caption:
OpenAI says a billing mistake at the GPT-6.2 launch discounted Astra and Sol usage for most users.
Now that it is fixed, the same work hits your limit about 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol.
As an apology, Go, Plus, Pro and Business users get one banked reset.

Is one reset a fair apology, or should OpenAI keep the old rate?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

paragraphs.text: OpenAI said it made a billing mistake when it launched its GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models, and that fixing it means paying subscribers will reach their usage limits sooner. OpenAI executive Thibault Sottiaux announced the correction on X on the evening of November 25, 2026, Pacific time, according to Implicator.ai and The Next Web.

According to the quote published by The Next Web, Sottiaux wrote that the mistake "incorrectly discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage for most users." He said the problem had been fixed, so the same work would now use more of a plan's usage allowance.

Compared with the first week after launch, OpenAI estimates that users will reach their limits about 40 percent faster on GPT-6.2 Astra and about 25 percent faster on GPT-6.2 Sol. Both models were released on November 17, 2026. Other models are not affected, and subscription prices did not change, The Next Web reported.

OpenAI will not charge users for the gap on usage that has already happened. Implicator.ai reported that a follow-up email described by one subscriber said past usage would not be recalculated and that paid credits were unchanged. The outlet also noted that OpenAI did not publish a matched before-and-after workload behind its percentages.
One banked reset as an apology

As compensation, OpenAI is adding one banked reset for everyone on the Go, Plus, Pro and Business plans. Implicator.ai reported that, according to OpenAI's help center, a reset restores the main Codex allowance for the plan, such as the five-hour and weekly limits on Plus and the weekly limit on Pro, and that at least one covered allowance must have less than 80 percent remaining before it can be used. The reset does not permanently raise any limit.

Reaction was mixed. The Next Web, citing TechRadar, reported that Reddit users were skeptical and that one called the single reset "pretty thin." Implicator.ai described a developer-forum user on a Pro plan who saw a weekly balance drop sharply during two parallel Astra sessions and asked OpenAI to show how much each thread and background task consumes.

The correction comes as OpenAI changes how ChatGPT limits work. The Next Web reported that Chat and Work will draw on a single usage allowance, a change that began for some Pro users and rolls out more broadly in December, according to OpenAI's support page. Chats with the Instant model stay unlimited and do not count toward the shared allowance. Sovereign Magazine reported that from December, Plus, Pro and Business plans will share one token-counted allowance across ChatGPT and Codex.
An OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch that most users should not hit limits more often under the shared system, while a small share of the heaviest users may, according to The Next Web.

For most casual subscribers the change may go unnoticed, but people who lean on Astra for long coding or research sessions in Work and Codex were effectively getting more usage than OpenAI intended during launch week. The fix brings their real allowance down to the level OpenAI planned, just as the company folds more of its products into one shared meter.
The next signal is December, when the shared Chat and Work allowance reaches more subscribers and heavy users will see how far one meter really stretches.
